raw_recipe.headline: Kabob Marinade
raw_recipe.description: This tasty kabob marinade with soy sauce, lemon, Worcestershire, mustard, and garlic is easy to make and great for grilled beef or chicken kabobs.
raw_recipe.name: Kabob Marinade

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk oil, soy sauce, lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, garlic, black pepper, and meat tenderizer together in a bowl until well combined.

review.reviewBody: This is a very simple and delicious marinade for beef kabobs. I cut the recipe in half for about 1.5 lbs. of meat. I used olive oil instead of veg.oil, low sodium soy sauce, and dijon for the prepared mustard. I left out the meat tenderizer, put everything into a ziploc bag and marinated it for over 24 hours. I skewered the meat separate from the peppers, onions, and cherry tomatoes as they cook at different rates. The meat was very tender and full of flavor - perfect with a side of rice.

Very good! Followed the recipe but just used regular black pepper, no meat tenderizer. Used boneless beef ribs cut into chunks. The meat came out very tender. Took advice from another recipe and heated the remainder of marinade to a boil in small saucepan, then simmered for 10 minutes and used to baste the meat & vegetables on the skewers while grilling. Will make it again.

Made the marinade two days before actually pouring over the kabobs. Skewered all meat and veggies together (I used portabella button mushrooms, green & red pepper, onions) and marinaded kabobs for 24+ hours. Grilled to perfection and turned out great. I left some marinading for an additional 24 hours and those tasted even better! Next time I make these I will definitely marinade these for 2 days as the meat was like butter! Excellent recipe! Thanks for sharing...........

I started following the recipe and after juicing 2 lemons I thought it was too tart. I was short of the amount called for, so I stopped with the juice of 2 lemons and added 3 T honey and 2-3 T sugar and omitted the meat tenderizer and instead used my manual meat tenderizer (has needles on a plunger that poke holes in the meat).

This makes a lot of marinade so I put about 1/3 in a bag and added red and orange peppers, vidalia onions, and thinly sliced zucchini. I cooked these in my grill basket.

I added the cubed meat in the bag with the other 2/3 of the marinade. 

Marinaded everything for 6+ hours and it was so delicious, kids went back for seconds :)

I use this for the recipe for vegetables and Rosemary Ranch Chicken Kabob marinade for the chicken. I use cherry tomatoes, onions, mushrooms, zucchini and red, yellow and green bell peppers. I marinate them in a gallon Ziploc for up to a day. Same as the Chicken. I skew the chicken and vegetables separately and BBQ on my Weber charcoal grill under indirect heat. I've been using these two recipes for several years for all kinds of events and it has been a hit every time. The two recipes accent each other.

used this marinade on half chickens ... roasted in the oven .. added a little brown sugar .. it was a great alternative to baking a stuffed chicken.. loved it . and it looked so good on the platter , sorry I did not take a picture....such a nice presentation! will make it for a dinner party some time soon.

Great marinade and flavor! We are printing the recipe to go into "the binder". Here's how we used it: 

We made sirloin (prime) kabobs with onions, peppers, mushrooms and squash. I halved the recipe and used olive oil. I also added some pepper paste (sembal oelek) to the tune of about 1/2 TBSP for a full recipe. I reserved about 1/4 to 1/2 cup of marinade to brush on the veggies and meat while grilling/turning. The meat marinated about 3-4 hours, that was enough time IMHO. Imagine 24 hours...

I used this marinade at a neighborhood BBQ. Everyone asked for the recipe. I did make a few changes. I used 1/2 cup vegetable oil and 1/2 cup olive oil. I did not add the meat tenderizer. I marinaded my meat and vegetable in different bags and then used the extra veg marinade to brush as the kabobs cooked. Delicious!

This was excellent! I only marinated the meat for 30 minutes and then brushed the marinade on the meat while it grilled. The flavor was awesome! I actually took a half a bite, went "wow" and then made my fiancee eat the other half of the bite in case I got an anomaly! It was excellent and has become part of our routine.

I made this for beef kabobs and added 1/4 cup of sweet chili sauce. I also used dijon mustard and let it marinate for 4 hrs. It was amazing. I drizzled a little bit of the marinade over skewers of mushrooms, onions, red and yellow peppers and yellow cherry tomatoes. Even my children who normally don't like any of the vegetables loved it. This is a new family favorite!
It’s my go to marinade recipe. Best thing about it is that I usually have all the ingredients already. I use it as a guideline and fudge a little bit when I have to.
Very good marinade. Not only did I do beef kabobs but chicken and even mushrooms. Definitely a keeper!
Excellent!!! I also marinated shrimp for 20 minutes for the shrimp and beef kabobs. Only change I made was to add a tablespoon of brown sugar. My husband LOVED it!

So flavorful! This does make quite a bit, even more than 2 pounds of meat. I feel the marinade would be too strong for a mild meat, like chicken or pork, but it works well with beef, and would be perfect for lamb too. I marinated cubed up piece of strip steak, and only did so for 2 hours. That was plenty, otherwise the flavor of the beef would have been lost. 24 hours would be way too long for my tastes. I also think the lemon juice would start breaking down/"cooking" the meat if left for that long. UPDATE: I used the marinade on chicken thighs and only marinated about 30 minutes. Even so, I felt the marinade overpowered the chicken. In the future I will only use this on beef, lamb or venison.
Great recipe, just as it is! Nothing in it that isn't for a purpose. Adding or omitting major ingredients, that's just a different recipe. I would suggest, do it if it must, but keep it to yourself.
Oh my gosh, this is excellent! Marinated the meat for 24 hours and omitted the meat tenderizer!! Thanks for this keeper!!

I did it just the way it was written but even with only a couple of hours marinate time, I found it to be too salty. Great flavor for sure and to clarify, I used dijon mustard, but next time I'll probably drop the soy to 1/2 a cup or even 1/4.

Made the recipe exactly as written, only I halved it for 1lb meat. I used stew meat and threw it in a plastic ziploc bag with all the marinade ingredients. I squeezed a lemon fresh. The only difference was I used Bragg’s aminos instead of soy sauce (tastes the same, just a healthier version), and Montreal steak seasoning instead of plain black pepper. I left out the meat tenderizer (it was optional) and Marinated in the fridge for 6 hours. I brushed my veggies with the marinade before cooking the kabobs. Everything was very flavorful!
It works. I cut everything by one half, because I did not have 2 pounds of beef.
